previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for a severe flare of right sacroiliac joint pain following a recent upper respiratory infection and initiation of Simponi therapy. He reported worsening pain after starting Simponi, along with fungal intertrigo in the right inguinal fold. He was treated with a three-day course of high-dose IV steroids, which significantly improved his pain without requiring an oral steroid taper. The intertrigo was managed with miconazole powder, and his home medications for hypertension, asthma, anxiety, and pain were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with rheumatology and infectious disease, continue Simponi, and monitor for recurrent symptoms.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MR LEFT HIP

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ankylosing spondylitis presenting with
possible flare with pain in left hip and sacroiliac joint, evaluate?any acute
pathology (ligamentous tear?)

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar multisequence routine MRI of the left hip without
intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON:  Sacroiliac joint radiographs ___, Hip radiographs
___

FINDINGS: 

Limited views of the right hip demonstrate a trace joint effusion, but are
otherwise unremarkable.

There is a small left hip joint effusion with probable associated synovitis. 
There is no fracture.  The femoral head is well-seated in the acetabulum. 
There is high linear signal within the anterosuperior labrum (series 8, image
21).  There is possible extension of signal abnormality to the anterior labrum
although artifact in this location somewhat limits evaluation.  There are no
suspicious bony lesions.  Muscle bulk is normal.  Gluteal and hamstring
insertions are unremarkable.  There is no greater trochanteric bursitis.

Limited views of the pelvic soft tissues are unremarkable.  Sacroiliac joints,
better evaluated on dedicated same-day study demonstrate fatty marrow
replacement most pronounced inferiorly.

IMPRESSION:


1. Small left hip joint effusion with synovitis.
2. Probable tear of the left anterosuperior labrum, possibly extending into
the anterior labrum.
3. The sacroiliac joints are better evaluated on dedicated examination
separately reported performed same day.
4. Trace right hip joint effusion.

EXAMINATION:  MRI of the Pelvis

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ankylosing spondylitis presenting with
possible flare with pain in the left hip and sacroiliac joint.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the sacroiliac joints.  Of note,
the patient was in too much pain to complete the examination and postcontrast
imaging was not obtained.

COMPARISON:  Sacroiliac joint MRI ___.

FINDINGS: 

Limited MRI examination secondary to patient pain without postcontrast, or
axial oblique STIR imaging.

Increased fatty marrow in the periarticular distribution in the bilateral
sacroiliac joints as well as bilateral sacroiliac erosive change is unchanged
from ___.  There remains minimal marrow edema in the inferior sacroiliac
joints, which has improved from prior.  No sacroiliac joint effusion is seen.

Note is made of fatty change in the anterosuperior corner of the S1 vertebral
body, also unchanged from ___.  Visualized pelvic soft tissues are normal.

IMPRESSION: 

Within the limitations of this examination, findings consistent with bilateral
chronic sacroiliitis, with minimal active inflammation of the inferior joint
spaces, improved from ___.
